% -------------------------------------------------
%  Dimensions of the grid (0‑indexed)
% -------------------------------------------------
n_rows(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Choose exactly one colour to be the wall colour.
%  The wall colour must be non‑zero and there must be at
%  least one interior (non‑reachable) zero cell.
% -------------------------------------------------
1 { is_wall(W) : color(W), W != 0 } 1 :- true.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  4‑connected neighbourhoods
% -------------------------------------------------
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Cells on the outer border of the grid
% -------------------------------------------------
border(R,C) :- R = 0.
border(R,C) :- R = NR - 1.
border(R,C) :- C = 0.
border(R,C) :- C = NC - 1.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Cells that are on the border and are NOT the wall colour
% -------------------------------------------------
border_start(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), border(R,C), not is_wall(V).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Cells reachable from the border through cells that are
%  not the wall colour (flood‑fill)
% -------------------------------------------------
outside(R,C) :- border_start(R,C,V), is_wall(W), V != W.
outside(R2,C2) :- outside(R1,C1), is_wall(W), input(R2,C2,V2), V2 != W,
                delta(DR,DC), R2 = R1 + DR, C2 = C1 + DC.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Output must be exactly one colour per cell
% -------------------------------------------------
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Transformation rules
% -------------------------------------------------
% Zero cells: reachable from the border keep 0,
%              interior become 4.
:- input(R,C,0), outside(R,C), output(R,C,Color), Color != 0.
:- input(R,C,0), not outside(R,C), output(R,C,Color), Color != 4.

% Non‑zero cells keep their original colour.
:- input(R,C,V), V != 0, output(R,C,Color), Color != V.

% At least one interior zero must exist (forces the correct wall colour)
1 { interior(R,C) : input(R,C,0), not outside(R,C) } 1 :- true.

<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  Input → Output transformation
%  The rule is:
%    • Colour 3 acts as a solid wall.
%    • Zeros that are reachable from the outer border through non‑3 cells

%    • Colour 3 cells stay 3.
%    • Every other non‑zero, non‑3 colour (6, 8, …) stays unchanged.
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  The puzzle is encoded as an exact‑one answer set.
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  Grid dimensions (0‑indexed)
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
min_row(R)  :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R)  :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C)  :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C)  :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  4‑connected neighbours
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  Outside region = non‑3 cells that can be reached from any border cell

outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  Input → Output transformation
%  The rule is:
%    • Colour 3 acts as a solid wall.
%    • Zeros that are reachable from the outer border through non‑3 cells
%      stay 0.
%    • Zeros that are *not* reachable (i.e. enclosed by colour‑3) become 4.
%    • Colour 3 cells stay 3.
%    • Every other non‑zero, non‑3 colour (6, 8, …) stays unchanged.
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  The puzzle is encoded as an exact‑one answer set.
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  Grid dimensions (0‑indexed)
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
min_row(R)  :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R)  :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C)  :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C)  :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  4‑connected neighbours
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
delta(0, 1). delta(0, -1). delta(1, 0). delta(-1, 0).

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  Outside region = non‑3 cells that can be reached from any border cell
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% flood‑fill through cells that are not colour 3
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1 + DR, C2 = C1 + DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
%  Enforce the transformation
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
% colour‑3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% zero cells that are reachable from the border stay 0
:- input(R, C, 0), outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% interior zeros (enclosed by 3’s) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.

% non‑zero, non‑3 cells keep their original colour
:- input(R, C, V), V != 0, V != 3, output(R, C, Color), Color != V.

The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>

output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.

outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
